blindSummary:
This state/province sits a small margin below the national average on the strength of one prominent case and its institutional aftermath, with the single-incident caveat applied explicitly. A 23-year-old transgender service member was found dead at her home in the state/province's administrative capital on 3 March 2021 (apparent suicide) following forced military discharge, while receiving ongoing mental-health counselling at a centre near her residence. Initial police and armed-forces handling classified the death as "natural"; this was overturned only three years later (April 2024), when a central review board of the defence ministry recognised it as service-related. The wrongful initial classification is the evidence: it reflects an institutional denial of the connection between anti-trans policy and a trans person's death, corrected only after sustained advocacy.

By the single-incident rule, one death cannot establish a pattern here, and no repeat-violence data exists for this unit. It is counted slightly below average rather than neutral because the state/province is small enough for one nationally prominent case to carry weight, and because the institutional response - a wrongful classification sustained for three years before correction - is a state-implicated finding. A neighbouring state/province hosts the positive court ruling that corrected the same institution's error, so this unit's share of the case is purely negative; the deviation nonetheless matches the neighbour's, because the correction (a court there, plus the defence review board) already mitigates the initial harm.
